hypothesis: Household income shock should precede mora onset.
evidence: Personal+cards mora rises Jan→Apr 2018 before May wage-shock anchor.
interpretation: Credit cycle/origination/macro conditions were already deteriorating; May is not an exogenous start of delinquency.

hypothesis: Mora should rise before provisions if provisions react only to observed household delinquency.
evidence: Adjusted coverage jumps 90.4%→113.2% in Dec-2023; material personal+cards mora acceleration begins Feb-2025.
interpretation: Provisioning responds to broader portfolio risk, regulation/accounting, expectations and non-household exposures too.

hypothesis: Bank profitability drawdown should follow household mora if mora is the dominant bank-stress channel.
evidence: ROA crosses below III23 benchmark in III24; material mora acceleration appears in early 2025.
interpretation: Valuation, rates, margins, balance-sheet changes and regulation matter before delinquency peaks.

hypothesis: Provision ratios should rise after mora if buffer use means building provisions.
evidence: Family mora rises 2.6→3.2 while headline coverage declines ~144→138% but net exposure stays negative.
interpretation: A high pre-existing buffer can be used without an increasing coverage ratio.

hypothesis: Same transmission chain should appear after all major shocks.
evidence: 2008 lacks the same immediate household wage onset under V31.

hypothesis: A single mora onset date is objective.
evidence: 2023 gives +3m at sustained +0.1pp but +14m at +0.3/+0.5pp; early rise later reverses.
interpretation: Report several thresholds and distinguish wiggle from material acceleration.
